cta_text.description: Fix cycle 3 item 4: the ONE CTA button text for this page. Must be exactly one of this schema's top-level allowed_cta_texts, with {short_name} filled in with the product's short model name (fix cycle 58). The renderer reuses it verbatim in the buy panel, the closing CTA and the phone bar -- choose it once here, never repeat/vary it elsewhere.

cta_url.description: The CTA's destination URL, reused everywhere cta_text is.

hero.description: The buy panel's writer lines: product name, the one-line promise, price, financing line, hero image.

promise.description: The one line under the model name in the buy panel, 4-10 words, sentence case: the ad's main point, said about the product in plain words (e.g. 'A two-person cedar sauna with the price on the page'). Keep it descriptive, not a numeric claim -- put any number/price/percent in price_line or financing_line instead; if the promise must state one, cite it in hero.claim_ids (the gate fails an uncited number here). This cartridge has no separate `headline` field -- the simplicity gate (harness/simplicity.py) measures this field's word count against this schema's own headline_word_band.

claim_ids.description: Claim ids backing hero.promise. Only needed when the promise states a number, price, percentage or trigger word; omit otherwise.

price_line.description: e.g. text: '$8,250'. Only add a compare-at/'was $X' figure if facts_pack.product.compare_at_price is non-null. Must carry the product's price claim_id.

financing_line.description: text: must be exactly the allowed financing sentence given in the prompt's Financing rule, verbatim -- never a freeform monthly figure, APR, or lender name typed in directly here, whether or not facts_pack.product.financing.lender is set.

angle_section.description: The promise band under the buy panel: one heading and exactly 2 short paragraphs that carry the ad's angle -- what the ad said, then what this product does about it.

paragraphs.description: Exactly 2 paragraphs, at most 45 words each.

attributed_to_customer.description: True only if this paragraph states a number that comes solely from the ad speaker's own estimate/hedge (ad_brief.speaker_experience), phrased as her own words, never as a brand fact and never carrying a claim_id. Never true anywhere else in this schema (never on a heading, an included item or an FAQ answer).

image.description: Optional. One asset_id from facts_pack.assets shown beside the paragraphs -- a lifestyle or installation photo, different from the hero.

included.description: 3-6 items for the 'What's included' list: what comes with the sauna, each a plain noun phrase of at most 8 words, sentence case (e.g. 'Full-body red light panel', 'Two Bluetooth speakers'). Each item is ONE verified claim with at least one claim_id from facts_pack.verified_claims. At least 3 of the claim_ids must be product-benefit claims -- what the sauna does or is built with -- not price, shipping-policy, warranty-terms, or returns-policy; the gate fails the page otherwise.

faq.description: Exactly 5 questions a visitor who clicked THIS ad asks before buying, answered from verified facts. Every answer that states a fact (a number, a price, a spec, or one of the trigger words) carries claim_ids.

answer.description: 1-2 sentences, at most 35 words. Answer the question first, then the detail.

gallery_order.description: Optional. Up to 5 asset_id strings (plain strings, not objects) from facts_pack.assets, in the order the product gallery should show them after the hero image. Omit to let the renderer order the product's own storefront images.
